stories.title: Tanker hit by projectile, disabled off Oman — UKMTO
stories.summary: LONDON, August 25. An oil tanker was damaged and left not under command in an attack off the coast of Oman, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said. "UKMTO has received a report of an incident 9NM northeast of Ash Shishah, Oman. The Master of an oil tanker reports the vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile causing damage to the engine room and disabling the vessel," the organization said. According to UKMTO, the crew are safe and no environmental impact has been reported. No further details, including the vessel's name and port of registry, were provided.

stories.title: S. Korea to develop environmental, ocean observation satellite
stories.summary: South Korea will develop a next-generation environmental and ocean observation satellite by 2033 to succeed the current geostationary satellite, the country's space agency said Tuesday. The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) said the proposal to develop the Cheollian-6 satellite has passed a preliminary feasibility review for a state-funded research and development project. The proposed satellite is scheduled for launch in 2033, with an estimated budget of about 770 billion won (US$556.7 million). It will take over the observation missions of Cheollian 2B, which was launched in 2020. Cheollian-6 will be tasked with monitoring the environment and oceans, enabling authorities to more quickly detect and track air and marine pollution as well as maritime disasters. The geostationary satellite will be developed using homegrown technologies, including a hybrid propulsion system. It will also be equipped with instruments capable of simultaneously conducting both environmental and ocean observations from a fixed position relative to the Earth, according to KASA.
